newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fischler to resubmit wheat tax proposal Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Fischler to resubmit wheat tax proposal Wednesday.

text.p: European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler is due on Wednesday to resubmit a proposal to tax daily exports of wheat grain and flour, a European Commission official said on Monday.
The proposal was suspended last Wednesday after French EU Commissioner Edith Cresson objected.

"It will probably go to the Commission on Wednesday," the commission official said, adding that the proposal for taxes of 15 Ecus a tonne on soft wheat grain and 20 Ecus on wheat flour would not be altered.
The EU's 20 commissioners will discuss the proposal and decide by majority vote.
Previously the proposal had been circulated to the commissioners for approval under the so-called written procedure, which required unanimity.
The tax is aimed at saving scarce supplies for EU domestic consumers and dampening prices, which have surged on fears of smaller world crops following frost in the U.S. and dry weather in Europe.

EU sources said last week that Cresson opposed the tax, saying it was no longer needed because world wheat prices had since fallen and there was no longer a danger of a flood of European wheat abroad.
France, the EU's main wheat exporter, has lobbied to maintain the flow of wheat shipments.
